Not quantified by a listed feature.

act_mean z +34.6 value 0.861 vs DMSO 0.28 at 0.3uM and z +57.8 value 1.251 at 3.0uM; act_std z +66.9/+168.7 and act_glcm_contrast z +50.3/+119.3. Composite-visible increase in mean intensity, variance and contrast agrees.

nuc_major_axis z -17.3 value 31.2 vs 36.8 at 0.3uM and z -30.3 value 26.9 at 3.0uM = smaller nuclei; nuc_solidity z -34.1/-55.3 value 0.964/0.959 vs 0.973 = less solid/regular outline; frac_mitotic_like z +20.1 value 0.098 vs 0.015 at 0.3uM and z +86.8 value 0.37 vs 0.015 at 3.0uM = large increase in rounded mitotic-like cells. extreme phenotype at 3.0uM: fewer cells, nearly all contracted bright yellow with spiky green protrusions and condensed blue nuclei, 37% mitotic-like

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: cytochalasin D - Actin disruptors. Submitted: Microtubule stabilizers p=0.52 - incorrect.

What the evidence got right - and misread:
- Dose-dependent increase in frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 (e9) over 4 wells/doses, nuc_solidity z=-48.9 and frac_mitotic_like z=+17.4 at low dose 0.03uM (e6), and density lower vs DMSO on microscopy (e4, e19) were real. I correctly noted a cell-cycle/condensation phenotype, but over-interpreted it as microtubule-stabilizer-induced mitotic arrest.
- Massive actin and tubulin texture increases were the dominant quantitative signal: act_std z=+66.9 (e2), +168.7 (e3), +139.0 (e7); tub_glcm_contrast z=+38.5 (e2) to +140.0 (e3) and +138.7 (e7); act_glcm_contrast z=+50.3 to +119.3; tub_mean rho=+1.00 (e10) and act_mean rho=+0.80 (e13). This should have pointed directly to actin disruption with secondary cell rounding/contraction driving apparent tubulin intensity/texture increases. Instead hypotheses update step 12 listed Actin disruptors as contradicting e10/e4/e9 and set p=0.08, while Microtubule stabilizers was supported by same e2/e3/e7/e9/e10.
- compare_to_reference_atlas did contain the correct signal but I discounted it: NSC vote Cholesterol-lowering 1/2 and 2/4 (e5,e8), k-neighbour Eg5 inhibitors 4-5/10, but also Actin disruptors 2/10 (e5) and 1/10 (e8) and Cholesterol-lowering 3/10. The atlas split indicated no confident microtubule stabilizer match, which I rationalized as 'outweighs split NSC vote' in the submitted conclusion.
- describe_phenotype candidates: Microtubule stabilizers (e4 on 2 fields, e19 on 3 fields) was taken as confirmatory. The reviewer's unblinded critique explains why: at 10uM the Oregon Green tubulin becomes coarse and punctate and H2B highly condensed without matching nuclear phenotype, consistent with EB3 amplification without nucleation of ring asters or increased nucleated microtubules - i.e. not a stabilized bundle/monoaster pattern. I had no 10uM data to see this.

Why I was misled - acquisition and comparison choices:
- Sampling plan: acquired 0.03uM (e6), 0.3uM (e2), 1uM (e7), 3uM (e3) - 4 of 4 wells left initially (e1) to 0 of 4 left (e18). I prioritized mid-range dose-response for frac_mitotic_like/tub_mean/nuc_area and missed the high-dose 10uM replicate 2 well the reviewer explicitly requested to score comet-bearing vs ring-aster vs bipolar-array cells. Step 18 budget-exhausted error prevented the requested experiment, and the proxy re-scoring of 0.03-3uM fields (e19) could not rescue it.
- Dose-response integration was incomplete: tub_mean increase (e10) was used to favor stabilizers over destabilizers, but I did not critically test whether act_mean/act_std/tub_glcm_contrast increases were primary actin effects vs secondary rounding. Negative/weak trends that contradict classic microtubule/Aurora arrest - nuc_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e11), frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e15), nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.60 p=0.4 (e16), cell_count rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e14) - were treated as exclusion of Aurora/destabilizer rather than reconsidering microtubule stabilizer itself.
- update_hypotheses anchoring: step 12 set Microtubule stabilizers 0.52, Eg5 0.20, Cholesterol-lowering 0.08, Actin 0.08 using e4/e9/e10 as support. Step 20 retained 0.52 despite e18 budget block and without new discriminating data. lookup_compound (e22,e23) returned 'none curated (name only)' and search_literature for 'cytochalasin D actin disruptor mechanism' (12 hits, e24) and for actin disruptor mitotic arrest rounding (0 hits, e25) returned no literature to correct the database gap, so name-only identity check was not used to raise the prior on actin.

Learning for next screen: when act_std/act_glcm_contrast z>50-100 exceed tubulin signals, and actin and tubulin both rise dose-dependently with condensed nuclei but without multinucleation/DNA content gains, prioritize actin disruptor orthogonal tests - phalloidin actin polymerization imaging and EB3-GFP comet vs tubulin ring-aster scoring at 10uM - before concluding microtubule stabilization. Budget must reserve high-dose wells for requested morphology.
This reflection is for cell-biology screening data interpretation only, not clinical advice.
what_was_right: frac_mitotic_like dose-dependent increase and low-dose solidity/condensation changes were real (e6,e9)
tubulin and actin texture/intensity increases were large and dose-related (e2,e3,e7,e10,e13)
what_was_wrong: Attributed act_std +168.7 and tub_glcm_contrast +140.0 to microtubule stabilization/rounding secondary rather than primary actin disruption
Overweighted microscopist Microtubule stabilizers candidates (e4,e19) and discounted atlas Actin disruptor neighbors (e5,e8)
Maintained p=0.52 after budget exhausted (e18) and without 10uM comet vs ring-aster data
reflection.next_experiment: High-dose 10uM replicate actin staining plus EB3-GFP comet quantification vs tubulin grayscale spindle/aster classification as requested, plus in vitro actin polymerization assay.

- Massive actin and tubulin texture increases were the dominant quantitative signal: act_std z=+66.9 (e2), +168.7 (e3), +139.0 (e7); tub_glcm_contrast z=+38.5 (e2) to +140.0 (e3) and +138.7 (e7); act_glcm_contrast z=+50.3 to +119.3; tub_mean rho=+1.00 (e10) and act_mean rho=+0.80 (e13). This should have pointed directly to actin disruption with secondary cell rounding/contraction driving apparent tubulin intensity/texture increases. Instead hypotheses update step 12 listed Actin disruptors as contradicting e10/e4/e9 and set p=0.08, while Microtubule stabilizers was supported by same e2/e3/e7/e9/e10.
- compare_to_reference_atlas did contain the correct signal but I discounted it: NSC vote Cholesterol-lowering 1/2 and 2/4 (e5,e8), k-neighbour Eg5 inhibitors 4-5/10, but also Actin disruptors 2/10 (e5) and 1/10 (e8) and Cholesterol-lowering 3/10. The atlas split indicated no confident microtubule stabilizer match, which I rationalized as 'outweighs split NSC vote' in the submitted conclusion.
- describe_phenotype candidates: Microtubule stabilizers (e4 on 2 fields, e19 on 3 fields) was taken as confirmatory. The reviewer's unblinded critique explains why: at 10uM the Oregon Green tubulin becomes coarse and punctate and H2B highly condensed without matching nuclear phenotype, consistent with EB3 amplification without nucleation of ring asters or increased nucleated microtubules - i.e. not a stabilized bundle/monoaster pattern. I had no 10uM data to see this.

Why I was misled - acquisition and comparison choices:
- Sampling plan: acquired 0.03uM (e6), 0.3uM (e2), 1uM (e7), 3uM (e3) - 4 of 4 wells left initially (e1) to 0 of 4 left (e18). I prioritized mid-range dose-response for frac_mitotic_like/tub_mean/nuc_area and missed the high-dose 10uM replicate 2 well the reviewer explicitly requested to score comet-bearing vs ring-aster vs bipolar-array cells. Step 18 budget-exhausted error prevented the requested experiment, and the proxy re-scoring of 0.03-3uM fields (e19) could not rescue it.
- Dose-response integration was incomplete: tub_mean increase (e10) was used to favor stabilizers over destabilizers, but I did not critically test whether act_mean/act_std/tub_glcm_contrast increases were primary actin effects vs secondary rounding. Negative/weak trends that contradict classic microtubule/Aurora arrest - nuc_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e11), frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e15), nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.60 p=0.4 (e16), cell_count rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e14) - were treated as exclusion of Aurora/destabilizer rather than reconsidering microtubule stabilizer itself.
- update_hypotheses anchoring: step 12 set Microtubule stabilizers 0.52, Eg5 0.20, Cholesterol-lowering 0.08, Actin 0.08 using e4/e9/e10 as support. Step 20 retained 0.52 despite e18 budget block and without new discriminating data. lookup_compound (e22,e23) returned 'none curated (name only)' and search_literature for 'cytochalasin D actin disruptor mechanism' (12 hits, e24) and for actin disruptor mitotic arrest rounding (0 hits, e25) returned no literature to correct the database gap, so name-only identity check was not used to raise the prior on actin.

Learning for next screen: when act_std/act_glcm_contrast z>50-100 exceed tubulin signals, and actin and tubulin both rise dose-dependently with condensed nuclei but without multinucleation/DNA content gains, prioritize actin disruptor orthogonal tests - phalloidin actin polymerization imaging and EB3-GFP comet vs tubulin ring-aster scoring at 10uM - before concluding microtubule stabilization. Budget must reserve high-dose wells for requested morphology.
This reflection is for cell-biology screening data interpretation only, not clinical advice.

What was right:
- frac_mitotic_like dose-dependent increase and low-dose solidity/condensation changes were real (e6,e9)
- tubulin and actin texture/intensity increases were large and dose-related (e2,e3,e7,e10,e13)

What was wrong or missed:
- Attributed act_std +168.7 and tub_glcm_contrast +140.0 to microtubule stabilization/rounding secondary rather than primary actin disruption
- Overweighted microscopist Microtubule stabilizers candidates (e4,e19) and discounted atlas Actin disruptor neighbors (e5,e8)
- Maintained p=0.52 after budget exhausted (e18) and without 10uM comet vs ring-aster data

Proposed next experiment: High-dose 10uM replicate actin staining plus EB3-GFP comet quantification vs tubulin grayscale spindle/aster classification as requested, plus in vitro actin polymerization assay.
